soft_deny: In ~/git/nixerator, these `just` recipes remain gated (require explicit review) because each runs `sudo` and/or a raw system mutation directly, bypassing the `just qr`/`just qu` safety wrappers (capture/backup/revert-on-failure): `rebuild`, `upgrade`, `hyprflake-test`, `bump-upsight`, `bump-hyprflake` (raw `sudo nixos-rebuild switch`); `clean`/`gc` (`sudo nix-collect-garbage`); `gc-nuclear` (multiple `sudo` mutations plus `rm -rf ~/.cache/nix` -- the most destructive recipe in the repo); `generations`/`gen` (`sudo`, read-only); `rollback`/`rb` (`sudo nixos-rebuild --rollback switch`); `remote-rebuild`/`rr` and `remote-upgrade`/`ru` (ssh into another host and trigger a rebuild there).

In ~/git/hyprflake, these `just` recipes remain gated: `pull-conflict` (runs `sudo tailscale down`/`up` around a git pull); `reset-hard` (`git reset --hard` + `git clean -fd`, discards local changes); `clean-all` (runs `nix-collect-garbage -d`).

In ~/git/homelab, these `just` recipes remain gated because they apply, destroy, or otherwise mutate the live Kubernetes/Talos homelab cluster with no confirmation of their own: `provision::apply`, `provision::apply-now`, `provision::destroy` (Terraform/OpenTofu apply or destroy against the live cluster); `grafana::apply`, `grafana::apply-now` (Terraform apply against live Grafana Cloud monitoring); `fleet::apply-all` (applies every cluster in the fleet unattended); `lifecycle::upgrade-node`, `upgrade-talos`, `upgrade-k8s`, `upgrade-cilium`, `apply-config` (upgrades/reconfigures live cluster nodes); `lifecycle::reset-node` (wipes a live node back to maintenance mode); `workloads::apply-manifests`, `setup-cert-manager`, `cert-manager-secret`, `setup-nfs-csi`, `bootstrap-eso-token`, `setup-observability` (applies manifests or rotates secrets on the live cluster); `flux::reconcile`, `suspend-kustomization`, `resume-kustomization`, `suspend-helmrelease`, `resume-helmrelease`, `bootstrap-flux-deploy-key` (controls live GitOps reconciliation or rewrites Flux's deploy-key secret); `image::fetch-iso` (uses `sudo` to install a downloaded ISO onto the host filesystem).
In ~/git/upsight, `release` and `quiet-release` remain gated -- they push commits/tags and publish a real public GitHub release.
In ~/git/nixerator: `just rebuild`, `just upgrade`, `just hyprflake-test`, `just bump-upsight`, `just bump-hyprflake` (raw `sudo nixos-rebuild switch`, bypassing the qr/qu wrappers)

In ~/git/nixerator: `just clean`/`gc`, `just gc-nuclear` (sudo nix-collect-garbage, including `rm -rf ~/.cache/nix`), `just rollback`/`rb`, `just remote-rebuild`/`rr`, `just remote-upgrade`/`ru` (remote host mutation via ssh)

In ~/git/donkeykong, these `just` recipes remain gated: `bootstrap` and `all` (full machine setup, installs packages and edits system settings); `update` (brew upgrade plus every package group); `macos` (rewrites macOS defaults); `touchid` (runs `sudo` to edit /etc/pam.d); `dotfiles::apply` (chezmoi overwrites files in $HOME); `containers::docker-down`, `containers::k3d-down` and `containers::k3d-recreate` (stop the Docker daemon or destroy local clusters). Read-only recipes (`doctor`, `dotfiles::diff`, `dev::check`, `dev::fmt`, `dev::test-scripts`, `containers::k3d-status`) are not gated.
